clue.text: Store model gains distinction

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store of goods
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T stands for a model

explanation.surface: A shop's new fashion range earns it a good reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store model' reads as a mannequin or shop design; it is really two separate pieces, a hoard and a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is prestige or a mark of excellence, a close synonym of distinction.

clue.text: Oberon, for example, not loud but cheerful

indicators.note: not loud tells the solver to do without the musical loud sign in the word

parts.note: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
f (forte) is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's fairy king, played quietly, comes across as jolly.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy manner is light-hearted and breezy, so the word works as a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Bellows below and drowns out the speaker

parts.note: to bellow is to howl loudly
down means lower down, below

explanation.surface: Someone roars from the floor below until a speaker can no longer be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To howl someone down is the idiom for shouting a speaker into silence.

clue.text: Toy with dessert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to play idly with something, treat it lightly
second meaning: a British pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a layered British pudding of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for treating something carelessly and the name of a cold layered pudding.

clue.text: Lose control on finding irregularity in flower

parts.note: a freak is an abnormality or aberration
flowers that are blooming are said to be out

explanation.surface: A gardener panics on spotting a deformed bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' tempts a river reading; here it is the plain bloom, and something in flower is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To freak out is an informal idiom for losing one's composure or panicking.

clue.text: No fun: has started spinning at very high speed

indicators.note: spinning letters are whirled around into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the mix
taken as written, the rest of the letters for the mix

explanation.surface: A joyless ride that has begun turning very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic travel outpaces sound, so the phrase describes extreme velocity.

clue.text: Thin slice of meat with stewed cole and peas

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down and mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; cole is an old word for cabbage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: a cut of meat served with cabbage and peas cooked slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole is an old word for cabbage, so the surface is a complete dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a boneless cutlet beaten flat, typically veal or pork.

clue.text: Understood to be present in empty kitchen

indicators.note: in places the time word inside the shell of the room
an empty kitchen keeps only its outer letters, its middle cleared

parts.note: only the first and last letters of kitchen stay once it is emptied
now is the present moment

explanation.surface: Something taken as read is there in a bare kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like 'here', but it is the time sense: the present is now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known is understood or recognised, the past participle of know.

clue.text: Full version of United Nations ban provided by journalist

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in 'the full version of a film'

parts.note: to censor is to suppress or ban material
ed, short for editor, is a stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: The UN bans a report, and a reporter supplies the complete text.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncensored text is complete, with nothing cut out by a censor.

clue.text: Cakes for little girls

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small squares of dense chocolate cake
second meaning: members of the junior Girl Guides, aged seven to ten

explanation.walkthrough: The Brownies are the youngest section of the Girl Guides, the British counterpart of Girl Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun names both chocolate traybakes and young members of the Guide movement.

clue.text: The pick of the finest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the selection made, the one chosen
second meaning: as an adjective, of top quality

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'the pick of the bunch', but splits into a noun sense and an adjective sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice is both the act or result of selecting and an adjective for superior quality.

clue.text: Another sinner initially leads vigil: a hopeful sign

indicators.note: another version of these letters means a different arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of leads
taken as written

explanation.surface: A second repentant wrongdoer heads a night watch, which offers hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters make another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cloud has a silver lining: the idiom names a consoling or hopeful aspect of misfortune.

clue.text: Attractive Nora upset over intellectual

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so comes first
upset means knocked over, so the name's letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
mental means of the intellect or mind

explanation.surface: Nora, a pretty woman, is annoyed with a brainy acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental things serve as decoration and are pleasing to look at.

clue.text: French bread left by Guevara, showing spirit

indicators.note: the bread is left behind by the revolutionary, who departs from it

parts.note: a brioche is a sweet French bread roll
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leaves behind a loaf, proving his zest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French bread' suggests a baguette or pain; it must be the roll that contains the revolutionary's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or vivacity, borrowed from Italian, and a synonym of spirit.

clue.text: Drink's round Dorothy's dog and all over

indicators.note: the drinking word goes round the dog, enclosing it

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily; the 's is 'is'
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A round of drinks goes to Dorothy's pet and everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: From top to toe is the idiom for completely, from head to foot.

clue.text: Frank has concluded that it has no limits

definitions.note: describes a thing; the answer is the adjective for such a thing

parts.note: frank and open both mean candid
ended means finished, concluded

explanation.surface: A candid person has decided that something is boundless.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-ended arrangement has no fixed end or limit.

clue.text: Everyone's convinced that it's now safe

definitions.note: the answer is the signal announcing this

parts.note: all means everyone; the 's is 'is'
to be clear about something is to be sure, convinced

explanation.surface: Everybody is sure the danger has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the siren or signal that danger, such as an air raid, is over.

clue.text: Mother I long to return to, taking a bloom

indicators.note: taking means the earlier pieces take on the last one at the end

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A homesick child longs to go back to mum, carrying a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blossoms.

clue.text: Steady the day before the start of negotiations

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Calm on the day before talks begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and steady both mean regular and unvarying, as in an even pace.

clue.text: Wood, twisted at the end, is of sound quality

indicators.note: only the last two letters of the wood word are twisted round

parts.note: timber is wood for building

explanation.surface: Warped wood can still give a fine tone, as with an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another.

clue.text: Having consequences concerning the echoing of drums?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
percussive describes the striking, resonant sound of drums

explanation.surface: A question of whether drums reverberating leads to effects.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the answer into 'about' and 'drum-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Repercussive means causing repercussions, effects that follow from an action.

clue.text: Time to find a goddess of poetry

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: An occasion to seek out a divine muse.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, one of nine minor goddesses.

clue.text: Part of pro-life article causes alarm

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters in these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of life and the start of article

explanation.surface: A piece of anti-abortion writing frightens readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and alarm are synonyms for sudden anxiety at danger.

clue.text: I quit the battle with a replacement to bombard from the air

indicators.note: the letter I quits, leaving its place in the word
another letter is brought in as a replacement for the one that left

parts.note: strife is conflict or struggle
the letter I itself
the letter A itself

explanation.surface: A soldier abandons the fight and a substitute arrives to attack from above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is read as the letter, not a speaker leaving the fray.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Without being asked, Ben undid knot

indicators.note: knot means to tie up in a tangle, so the letters are twisted together

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the mix

explanation.surface: Ben untied a knot of his own accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' reads as a noun after 'undid'; it is a verb telling you to tangle the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbidden means uninvited, done or arriving without a request.

clue.text: Radical descent first into the shade

indicators.note: first means the lineage word comes ahead of the political one

parts.note: blood means lineage, ancestry
red is slang for a political radical, a communist

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's family background is pushed into the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' reads as shadow but means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-red is a deep crimson, one colour among many shades.

clue.text: Stay for the last flower

parts.note: the end is the last part
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Waiting around for the final bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river; the Ure runs through Yorkshire in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to last or remain, as stay can mean to persist.
